questions.question: A is 192.0.2.10/24 and B is 203.0.113.25. Which IP address is the destination of A first SMTP data packet?
questions.explanation: A keeps the remote host as IP destination while addressing the local frame to a gateway.

source.section: Section 8 — IP addressing routing and forwarding

questions.question: Which mask corresponds to /24?
questions.explanation: The first 24 bits of this mask are ones.

source.section: Section 8 — IP addressing routing and forwarding

questions.question: Routes include a default, 203.0.0.0/16, 203.0.113.0/24, and 203.0.113.128/25. Which is selected for 203.0.113.25?
questions.explanation: The /25 does not cover .25, so /24 is the longest matching prefix.

source.section: Section 8 — IP addressing routing and forwarding

questions.question: Using those same routes, which is selected for 203.0.113.200?
questions.explanation: The address is in .128 through .255 and the /25 beats the other matching entries.

source.section: Section 8 — IP addressing routing and forwarding

questions.question: What is the main difference between routing and forwarding?
options: A) Routing parses SMTP; forwarding parses MIME
B) Routing builds path information; forwarding applies a local table decision to a packet
C) Routing is done by switches only; forwarding is done by applications only
D) Every packet performs a complete BGP calculation at every hop
questions.explanation: Control-plane path selection and data-plane packet handling are distinct.

source.section: Section 8 — IP addressing routing and forwarding

questions.question: Which IPv4 field normally decreases at a forwarding router?
questions.explanation: TTL limits forwarding loops; the IPv4 header checksum must reflect the changed header.

source.section: Section 8 — IP addressing routing and forwarding

questions.question: Which IPv4 Protocol value identifies TCP?
questions.explanation: The Protocol value is distinct from the TCP service port.

source.section: Section 8 — IP addressing routing and forwarding

questions.question: Which statement is correct for the IPv6 base header?
options: A) It is 20 bytes and has an IPv4-style checksum
B) It is 40 bytes and has no header checksum
C) It stores 48-bit source and destination addresses
D) It requires ARP for every destination
questions.explanation: IPv6 uses a fixed base header and different neighbor-resolution machinery.

source.section: Section 8 — IP addressing routing and forwarding

questions.question: What does an ordinary IPv6 router do with a packet too large for the outgoing link?
options: A) It does not fragment it; path-MTU feedback lets the source adapt
B) It always fragments it like IPv4 with DF clear
C) It changes the packet into a TCP SYN
D) It asks DNS to reduce the email size
questions.explanation: IPv6 source behavior and path-MTU handling replace router fragmentation.

source.section: Section 8 — IP addressing routing and forwarding

questions.question: A must reach a remote B and lacks its gateway mapping. Which address does it normally resolve with ARP?
options: A) The remote mailbox local part
B) The remote server MAC through Internet-wide broadcast
C) The local next-hop gateway IPv4 address
D) The destination DNS root server name
questions.explanation: ARP resolves a neighboring next hop on the current link.

source.section: Section 9 — ARP and IPv6 Neighbor Discovery

questions.question: How is an ARP request carried in the Ethernet example?
options: A) Inside a TCP packet with destination port 826
B) Inside DNS as an MX record
D) Directly in an Ethernet frame with EtherType 0x0806
questions.explanation: ARP does not use IPv4, TCP, or UDP encapsulation in this example.

source.section: Section 9 — ARP and IPv6 Neighbor Discovery

questions.question: What is the Ethernet destination for the ordinary broadcast ARP request?
options: B) The remote B MAC address
questions.explanation: The broadcast is confined to the relevant LAN or VLAN.

source.section: Section 9 — ARP and IPv6 Neighbor Discovery

questions.question: Which protocol family provides IPv6 Neighbor Solicitation and Advertisement?
questions.explanation: IPv6 Neighbor Discovery uses ICMPv6 and also supports router discovery and reachability.

source.section: Section 9 — ARP and IPv6 Neighbor Discovery

questions.question: What does address-and-port translation change in the common home-NAT example?
options: A) Packet source address and source port, with affected checksums adjusted
B) The complete SMTP message into a new application transaction
C) The recipient MX preference into the Ethernet FCS
D) Only the message Subject header
questions.explanation: NAT rewrites packet fields and tracks a mapping; it is not an SMTP relay.

source.section: Section 8 — IP addressing routing and forwarding

questions.question: How do DNS TTL and IP TTL differ?
options: B) DNS TTL concerns cached records; IP TTL limits packet forwarding
C) Both identify a TCP receive buffer
D) DNS TTL is always stored inside the IP header
questions.explanation: The same acronym refers to different scopes and units of operation.

source.section: Section 8 — IP addressing routing and forwarding

questions.question: What happens if the destination host is directly reachable in A own subnet and VLAN?
options: A) A must always send through the default gateway
B) A performs an Internet-wide ARP broadcast
C) A normally resolves the peer MAC and sends directly through the LAN
D) A changes SMTP to UDP
questions.explanation: A connected route can select direct local delivery instead of the gateway.
